column1: # THE DESTINATION BAR'S ADJUDICATION TABLE.  barledger.py --bar destination
# joins the family table from `dstbar.py --tsv` to these rows and REFUSES on
# any family that matches none, on any that matches two, and on any row here
# that matches nothing.  It is the SOURCE table's construction, applied to the
# WHAT THE DESTINATION BAR MEASURES.  Registers the WIRE publishes as
# DESTINATIONS that QEMU's write side does not name.  It is scored only where
# QEMU's own write verdict is complete, so a refusal is never counted as a
# loss -- the same discipline the source bar applies to its read verdict.
# THE THREE DISPOSITIONS ARE barledger.py's, unchanged, and the one that
# needed saying out loud is QEMU-STATES-IT.  On this side the commonest defect
# is not "the translation contains the write and the extraction does not carry
# it out" but "QEMU ELIDES a write the architecture defines" -- a self-move
# whose two operands coincide, a NOP arm that returns before the store.  The
# disposition covers both because the remedy is the same one, and the
# definition was GENERALISED in barledger.py rather than stretched in silence
# columns: class_id  isa  rule_rx  mnem_rx  reg_rx  disposition  citation  note

column7: target/i386/tcg/decode-new.c.inc, the reserved-NOP arms -- the operand is decoded and no store is emitted for it; Intel SDM, NOP: 'the ModR/M operand is ignored'
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: every losing register on these families is a ModRM-named GPR and the family carries no other. 4d9ec8775e ruled the operands a reserved NOP NAMES, which is why they are SOURCES; it says nothing about a result the instruction does not produce. Capstone marks the ModRM operand read/write and the WRITE half is the false one.

column7: target/i386/tcg/decode-new.c.inc VMOVLPx / VMOVHPx; Intel SDM MOVLPD/MOVHPD require mod != 3; binutils 2.45.1 renders `66 0F 12 /r` mod==3 as `movlpd (bad),%xmm0`
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, the SOURCE side's own and the same rows: 480/480 losing encodings carry the 66 prefix with mod == 3, an encoding the SDM declares INVALID. QEMU routes it to VMOVLPx and writes the r/m register; Capstone reads it as MOVHLPS and writes the reg register. The row measures a DECODER DISAGREEMENT on an architecturally invalid encoding, and no statement can close it: stating the write Capstone implies would agree with Capstone against both the SDM and QEMU.

column7: target/i386/tcg/decode-new.c.inc, the RDSSP arm; Intel SDM RDSSPD/RDSSPQ: 'If shadow stacks are not enabled ... this instruction is a NOP'
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: this model enables no shadow stack on any of the losing encodings, so the destination genuinely is not written and QEMU is right not to name it. NOT the same shape as the MPX class beside it, where the ISA defines the access regardless of whether the feature is present -- here the ISA itself makes the write conditional and the condition is false.

column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, the source side's own --field 3:0 arm over the same family: mask == 0 on 82 of 192 encodings, and 82 is exactly the destination bar's count. A flag outside the mask is a register the instruction does not write, so the wire's claim is the false one.

column7: target/arm/tcg/translate-a64.c handle_sys, the DC arms -- `dc zva` and its siblings write MEMORY through a helper and no cache register
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: every losing register on this family is REG_SYSCACHE and the family carries no other. column7: target/arm/tcg/translate-a64.c trans_ESB -- a NOP on a model with no RAS error records
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: one family, one register (REG_SYSEXC), every encoding. ESB synchronises error state; with no RAS errors implemented there is no error record to write, which is the RDSSP reading applied to the other architecture: the ISA makes the write conditional and the condition is false on this model.

column7: target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_rvzacas.c.inc trans_amocas_q -- `if (a->rd != 0)` guards BOTH halves of the pair write, and get_gpr() takes `a->rd == 0 ? 0 : a->rd + 1` on the read side
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, and it is the DESTINATION half of the source side's ruling: 100% of the losing encodings have rd == 0. column7: target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_rvzimop.c.inc -- Zimop writes 0 to x[rd] and defines no shadow-stack effect
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: every losing register on these families is REG_SSP and the families carry no other. The register belongs to the OTHER reading and QEMU is not implementing that one.

column7: target/riscv/translate.c -- an encoding that decodes ILLEGAL raises and reaches no gen_set_gpr()
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: every losing register on this family arrives on an encoding whose decode result is ILLEGAL, and a raise writes no GPR. The registers the wire names are the ones the ENCODING's bit fields would have selected had the encoding been legal, which is the reference reading an instruction that does not exist.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c gen_trap() -- the cond==0 arm for OPC_TLT/TLTI/TLTU/TLTIU/TNE/TNEI is `/* Never trap: treat as NOP. */ break;`, which emits NOTHING; MIPS64 Vol II defines these six as CONDITIONAL traps and the condition is rs<rs, rs!=rs or 0<0, which is false by inspection, so no exception is architecturally defined on this arm either
column8: RE-ADJUDICATED, AND THE PREVIOUS DISPOSITION NAMED A REMEDY THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN A FABRICATION.  QEMU-STATES-IT asks for a statement at the citation's site: here that would make QEMU say `tlt $t0,$t0` writes exception state, and it does not -- the arm is a NOP in the emulator BECAUSE the trap is a NOP in the architecture.  The old note's own words were the clue and were read the wrong way round: `exception state as a DESTINATION is what a RAISE does write` is true, and this arm does not raise.  WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, and it is a PROOF rather than a census: the never-trap arm is reachable ONLY at cond==0, and cond==0 holds for the register forms exactly when rs==rt and for the immediate forms exactly when rs==0 && imm==0 (translate.c, the two `if (rs != rt)` / `if (rs != 0 || imm != 0)` guards that set cond=1).  So the losing set is not a sample of the mnemonic -- it IS the fold condition, closed-form.  The immediate forms admit exactly ONE such encoding each and the bar reads exactly 1, 1, 1 on tlti/tltiu/tnei, which is that closed form agreeing with the measurement.  EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE BAR at verify67/barscore_out3: the six rules carry SIX rows, REG_SYSEXC and no other register, 36+36+36+1+1+1 = 111 encodings -- the whole of this class.  The always-trap siblings (TEQ/TGE/TGEU and their immediate forms) fall to generate_exception_end() in the same switch and are not in the bar, and the DYNAMIC arm (rs != rt) traps under a brcond and is not in the bar either: the split is by OPERANDS, not by mnemonic, which is why no (rule, mnemonic, register) pattern separates them and the reason is stated here instead.  NO WIRE SUBJECT AND NO WIRE CHANGE: the mech column reads UNPUBLISHED on all 111, so the family did not reach the wire in the tip corpus at all; the operand walk names REG_SYSEXC here and QEMU does not, and the deletion dropping it is a FABRICATION REMOVED, not information lost.  R12.1 is satisfied without discount: nothing real is lost, so nothing is being written off as a pessimistic direction.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c OPC_PMON -- gen_helper_pmon(tcg_env, sa); SPECIAL function 5 is PMON on this pre-R6 model and LSA only on Release 6
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, the source side's own and the same rows: this model does not have LSA, so it has no rd to write. The registers the wire names are operands of an instruction THIS MODEL DOES NOT HAVE. Stated as a QEMU-modeling fact and never as tracer scope, which is what the all-MIPS-models ruling requires.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c OPC_MUL -- the MIPS32 three-operand MUL writes rd and leaves HI/LO alone; MIPS32 ISA, MUL: 'the values of HI and LO are UNPREDICTABLE after the operation'
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: the two losing registers are REG_ACC0 and REG_ACCHI0 on every encoding of the family. An architecturally UNPREDICTABLE result is not a write the wire may claim and not one QEMU may be faulted for omitting: there is no value for a consumer to depend on, which is the whole content of the dependency the wire would be asserting.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c gen_movcf_* -- the `ft != 0` guard means the whole body is elided when the condition register is $zero
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, the destination twin of the source side's §1c: with ft == 0 the condition is settled at TRANSLATION time and `movn` never moves, so the destination is never written and the drop is RIGHT. The same reading a64-ccond-always carries: an operand the surviving arm never uses is not a dependency. `movz` with ft == 0 always moves and is not in this class.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c OPC_JALR -- `jr $ra` IS `jalr $zero,$ra`, and gen_store_gpr() discards a write to register 0
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM: one family, REG_LR, every encoding. The destination the encoding names is rd == $zero and the wire names $ra, which is the SOURCE the jump reads. A destination slot filled with the source register is the reference's own reading of the `jr` alias, not a write QEMU is missing.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c gen_cl -- QEMU writes cpu_gpr[rd] and the `rd == 0` arm writes nothing; MIPS32 CLZ/CLO: 'the rt field must be set to the same value as the rd field ... the result is UNPREDICTABLE if the rt and rd fields differ'
column8: THE QUESTION IS ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT AND THE ROW IS NOT BLOCKED ANY MORE. It asked which field the wire reads, which QEMU writes, and whether either reading is defensible where they differ. Measured over all 192 clz/clo rows of the tip corpus: QEMU writes rd on 144 of the 144 rows with rd != 0 and nothing on the 48 with rd == 0; the wire's PUBD is rd on 78 rows, rt on 58, and NEITHER on 54 -- there it names a register whose number is rt + rd, which is a field neither decoder has. WHOLE-POPULATION ARM on the architectural split: rt == rd on FOUR of the 192 encodings, and MIPS32 makes every other one UNPREDICTABLE by the restriction quoted above. 110 of the 112 losing registers are on those 188 undefined encodings, which is `mips-mul-acc-dst`'s sentence verbatim -- an architecturally UNPREDICTABLE result is not a write the wire may claim and not one QEMU may be faulted for omitting. The other 2 were `clz $zero,$rs` / `clo $zero,$rs`, rt == rd == 0, the one defined shape in the losing set: a REAL discarded write, and 209963934a states it at gen_cl's NOP arm with note_gpr_zero_dest(). SPLIT-ACK: no pattern over (rule, mnemonic, register) separates rt == rd from rt != rd, so the split is stated here rather than encoded, and the row is about the UNPREDICTABLE arm alone.

column7: target/i386/tcg/emit.c.inc gen_WRMSR / cpl0_operands.c.inc, the WRMSR arm -- EAX, ECX and EDX are stated and the MSR ECX selects is REFUSED; Intel SDM WRMSR: "Writes the contents of registers EDX:EAX into the 64-bit model specific register (MSR) specified in the ECX register"
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, and it is the source side's ruling read in the other direction: the WRMSR family's walk-only destination set is REG_SYS on 3 encodings and nothing else.  The three GPRs 8e394d789f states are the READ side of the same sentence and left the source bar with it; what is left is the destination the ECX selector picks at RUN TIME, which has no CPUArchState member, no range and no name.  REFUSING THE DESTINATION WHILE STATING THE SOURCE IS NOT THE MODEL CHOOSING WHICH HALF OF ONE DEFINITION TO BELIEVE, which is what 22d7666262 forbids: EDX:EAX and ECX have storage and names, the selected MSR has neither, and the split falls on that fact rather than on the direction.  The mirror row on the read side is `x86-msr-selected`, and rdmsr's EDX:EAX destinations are STATED rather than refused for the same reason -- they are registers this build has.

column7: target/mips/tcg/translate.c check_cp0_enabled() at :1877 and check_cp0_mt() at :2085 -- both open `if (unlikely(!(ctx->hflags & MIPS_HFLAG_CP0))) generate_exception_end(ctx, EXCP_CpU)`, and CU0 is clear at user level, which is where the sweep runs
column8: WHOLE-POPULATION ARM, BY INTERVENTION AND EXHAUSTIVE: every losing encoding of these families was put at the entry point of a minimal static ELF and run under `qemu-mipsel -d op,in_asm` at the sweep's own CPU model and privilege (trapstate_probe.py --isa mipsel, 24Kf, user mode), and QEMU's own TCG ops were read.  ALL 7,747 OF THEM ARE TRAP-ONLY -- the whole of what the translation does with the instruction is set the PC and call an exception helper.  No operand is read and no destination is written, so the registers the operand walk publishes here are the architectural destinations of an instruction that did not run: a fabrication removed, not information lost.  R12.1 is satisfied without discount.  The probe's two controls FIRED in this same run -- `addu $2,$3,$4` read DATAPATH and `mfc0 $2,$0` read TRAP-ONLY -- so the verdict is not an instrument stuck at one answer.  Evidence: cst_runs/exec190/adj/trapstate_mipsel.tsv (11,896 rows, 11,896 TRAP-ONLY).
